text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000093 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity tier, including simple acute visits, but too few charts came back to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward upcoding rather than a sicker panel. The 99215 share runs roughly two to four times the all-provider rate within every condition-count tier, including patients with no chronic conditions, so panel complexity does not explain the excess. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include rash, upper respiratory infection and follow-up-only visits (for example C0048909, C0049012, C0049082, C0049171), which are hard to square with high-level visits, while the high-complexity examples such as C0048901 and C0049386 look plausible. The documentation cannot settle the question: only 2 documented 99215 claims came back. Both supported the billed level, but one of them, C0048889, is a zero-condition rash visit documented as high MDM with no time recorded, so a reviewer should check whether that note is templated or cloned. As a first step, request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims and for a sample of the heavily used 99214 claims, then compare the documented MDM to the diagnoses on each claim."}
